topic: Tauri 2 platform capabilities and crate choices for RoALT (verified against tauri 2.12.5, wry 0.57.0, webview2-com 0.39.1, windows 0.62.2 source in the local cargo cache, plus crates.io, npm, Microsoft Learn and GitHub as of 2026-10-24)

findings.claim: Tauri 2 can read every cookie in an embedded WebView2, HttpOnly and Secure ones included. Webview::cookies() and cookies_for_url() were added in tauri 2.4.0; set_cookie() and delete_cookie() were added in 2.8.0. All four are in the current stable release, 2.12.5.
findings.detail: Versions: crates.io tauri max_stable_version 2.12.5 (published 2026-10-21). 3.0.0-alpha.5 also exists, so pin "2" and do not take the alpha. Changelog (raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/tauri/dev/crates/tauri/CHANGELOG.md): 2.4.0 'Adds Webview::cookies(), Webview::cookies_for_url(), and WebviewWindow::cookies()'; 2.8.0 'Adds Webview::set_cookie(), Webview::delete_cookie(), WebviewWindow::set_cookie() and WebviewWindow::delete_cookie()'. Doc comment in tauri-2.12.5/src/webview/mod.rs:2405: 'Returns all cookies in the runtime's cookie store including HTTP-only and secure cookies. Note that cookies will only be returned for URLs with an http or https scheme.' Signatures: pub fn cookies_for_url(&self, url: Url) -> crate::Result<Vec<Cookie<'static>>>; pub fn cookies(&self) -> ...; pub fn set_cookie(&self, cookie: Cookie<'_>) -> crate::Result<()>; pub fn delete_cookie(&self, cookie: Cookie<'_>) -> ...; pub fn clear_all_browsing_data(&self) (Windows: ICoreWebView2Profile2::ClearBrowsingDataAll; the deletion is asynchronous). The same methods exist on WebviewWindow. Cookie type: tauri::webview::Cookie re-exports cookie 0.18 (cookie 0.18.2 is the latest). Windows implementation (wry-0.57.0/src/webview2/mod.rs:1702-1753): ICoreWebView2_2::CookieManager()?.GetCookies(uri or null, GetCookiesCompletedHandler) followed by webview2_com::wait_with_pump. cookie_from_win32 reads IsHttpOnly, IsSecure, SameSite and Expires. Microsoft's ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies docs: 'If uri is empty string or null, all cookies under the same profile are returned.'

findings.claim: On Windows, cookies() and cookies_for_url() deadlock when called from a synchronous command or from an event handler. This includes the on_navigation and on_page_load closures. Call them from a separate thread or an async command (spawn_blocking). Creating a WebviewWindow from a synchronous command deadlocks for the same reason.
findings.detail: Doc comment, tauri 2.12.5 mod.rs:2439: 'On Windows, this function deadlocks when used in a synchronous command or event handlers, see [the Webview2 issue] (https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/583). You should use async commands and separate threads when reading cookies.' webview_window.rs:58 says the same about WebviewWindowBuilder::new. How it happens (tauri-runtime-wry-2.12.3/src/lib.rs): send_user_message runs the request inline when called on the main thread; otherwise it posts to the event loop and the caller blocks on rx.recv(). wry then pumps messages until WebView2's GetCookies callback fires, and that callback cannot fire while the main thread is inside another WebView2 callback. tauri-runtime-wry 2.11.3 (2026-06-17, PR #15504) fixed a separate case: 'cookies_for_url can cause deadlocks if called with another windowing/webview method'. Use tauri 2.11.3 or later; 2.12.5 is current. The call blocks its thread, so in async code wrap it in tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking.

findings.claim: Tauri's set_cookie and delete_cookie are not safe for injecting .ROBLOSECURITY. They drop the leading dot from the Domain (".roblox.com" becomes "roblox.com"), and WebView2 treats those as different domains. Both calls are fire-and-forget: they return Ok(()) and failures only go to log::error!.
findings.detail: set_cookie path: tauri-runtime-wry-2.12.3 lib.rs:1698 calls send_user_message(WebviewMessage::SetCookie) and returns Ok(()) straight away. The handler at lib.rs:3816 runs `if let Err(e) = webview.set_cookie(&cookie) { log::error!(...) }`. wry cookie_into_win32 (mod.rs ~1660) does `let domain = cookie.domain().map(HSTRING::from).unwrap_or_default(); cookie_manager.CreateCookie(&name,&value,&domain,&path)`. cookie 0.18.2 Cookie::domain() docs: 'if the Domain starts with a leading ., the leading . is stripped'. Microsoft ICoreWebView2Cookie::get_Domain: 'Note that, for instance, ".bing.com", "bing.com", and "www.bing.com" are considered different domains.' AddOrUpdateCookie: 'This method will fail if the domain of the given cookie is not specified.' Roblox itself sets domain cookies; see fixture tauri-www-login-setcookie-headers.json: 'GuestData=...; domain=.roblox.com', 'RBXEventTrackerV2=...; domain=roblox.com'. Inference, not tested at runtime: a cookie created through tauri with domain "roblox.com" is host-only and is not sent to www.roblox.com or the API subdomains. Reading cookies back through tauri also strips the dot, so you cannot tell host-only from domain cookies. The capture value is unaffected.

findings.claim: To inject cookies correctly and change WebView2 settings that Tauri does not expose, go to ICoreWebView2CookieManager directly through Webview::with_webview. The app's webview2-com and windows dependencies must be the same versions Tauri 2.12 uses (0.39 and 0.62).

Isolation options in Tauri 2.12.5: WebviewWindowBuilder has data_directory, incognito, additional_browser_args, devtools, general_autofill_enabled and proxy_url. WebView2 profile names, default context menus and browser accelerator keys are not exposed; set those through with_webview. If no data_directory is given on Windows, Tauri uses app_local_data_dir().
findings.detail: webview_window.rs: additional_browser_args (line 1080), data_directory(PathBuf) (1089), incognito(bool) (1119), browser_extensions_enabled, devtools(bool) (1232; on by default in debug builds, release builds need the `devtools` cargo feature), general_autofill_enabled, cookies, clear_all_browsing_data. incognito doc: 'Windows: Requires WebView2 Runtime version 101.0.1210.39 or higher, does nothing on older versions.' wry implements it with ICoreWebView2ControllerOptions::SetIsInPrivateModeEnabled (mod.rs:414). additional_browser_args warning: 'Webview instances with different browser arguments must also have different data directories... By default wry passes --disable-features=msWebOOUI,msPdfOOUI,msSmartScreenProtection so if you use this method, you also need to disable these components by yourself.' wry 0.57 has WebViewBuilderExtWindows::with_profile_name, with_default_context_menus and with_browser_accelerator_keys, but a grep of tauri 2.12.5 and tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3 finds no use of profile_name or default_context_menus. Default data directory (tauri manager/webview.rs:559-569): 'in windows, we need to force a data_directory' → app_local_data_dir(), created if missing; WebView2 writes EBWebView under it. tauri-runtime-wry caches one WebContext per data_directory key and, on Windows, drops it when the last webview using it is dropped (lib.rs:2392-2416). The main window can disable its context menu itself with a JS contextmenu preventDefault.

findings.claim: How WebView2 user data folders (UDFs) behave: each UDF is one browser session (its own msedgewebview2 process group), and one app can use several. Webviews sharing a UDF must use identical environment options. A UDF cannot be deleted while its session is alive. InPrivate is an off-the-record profile derived from the regular one, so incognito windows in the same UDF probably share one InPrivate cookie jar. For strict per-account isolation, give each login or session window its own temporary data_directory.
findings.detail: Microsoft Learn 'Manage user data folders' (ms.date 2026-06-26): 'Each WebView2 session has exactly one UDF. A UDF can only have at most one WebView2 session at a time.' 'Each WebView2 browser process consumes additional memory and disk space. Therefore, avoid running a WebView2 control with too many different UDFs at the same time.' 'To delete a user data folder (UDF), you must first end the WebView2 session.' '...wait for the browser process and all child processes to exit before deleting the UDF... use the BrowserProcessId property.' Option mismatch: per the ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions2 docs (seen via a search summary and a mirror, not read on the primary page), creating an environment for an in-use UDF with different options (language, ExclusiveUserDataFolderAccess, extra arguments) fails with HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_INVALID_STATE). Multi-profile docs: profiles share one UDF and browser process; ProfileName allows ASCII letters, digits and #@$()+-_~. and space, up to 64 characters, case-insensitive, and must not end in '.' or space. Tauri does not expose ProfileName (T5), so per-session isolation in Tauri means a separate data_directory. InPrivate: Microsoft's profile docs say an InPrivate webview gets 'an off-the-record profile (an InPrivate profile) from a regular profile'. That two concurrent incognito windows in the same UDF share cookies follows from Chromium's off-the-record design and was NOT tested. Cleanup: read BrowserProcessId through with_webview before closing (T4), destroy the window, then OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE) on that PID, WaitForSingleObject with a timeout, and std::fs::remove_dir_all with retries. On startup, sweep stale temp UDFs.

findings.claim: Detecting that login finished: the available hooks are on_navigation (allow or deny), on_page_load (Started and Finished, with the URL), on_document_title_changed and on_new_window. All of them run on the main thread inside WebView2 callbacks, so they may only signal a worker. The most reliable check is a worker thread that polls cookies_for_url(https://www.roblox.com/) until .ROBLOSECURITY appears; a URL change to /home only speeds it up. Remote pages get no IPC by default.
findings.detail: tauri 2.12.5 webview_window.rs: on_navigation<F: Fn(&Url) -> bool + Send + 'static> (line 266; return false to cancel the navigation); on_page_load<F: Fn(WebviewWindow<R>, PageLoadPayload<'_>)> (421); PageLoadPayload::url() and ::event() -> PageLoadEvent::{Started, Finished}; on_document_title_changed and on_new_window are in mod.rs:592/601. WebviewWindow::url() can be polled. Flow: create the window from an async command with WebviewUrl::External("https://www.roblox.com/login".parse()?). A worker thread (std::thread or spawn_blocking) loops every 500-1000 ms: webview.cookies_for_url("https://www.roblox.com/".parse()?)? and find(|c| c.name()==".ROBLOSECURITY" && !c.value().is_empty()). on_page_load(Finished) with url.path() starting "/home" only wakes the worker early through a channel. Single-page history.pushState changes do not trigger NavigationStarting, so URL hooks alone are not enough. Capabilities (v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities): 'By default the API is only accessible to bundled code shipped with the Tauri App'; remote origins need a capability with "remote": {"urls": [...]}. Do not give the login-* windows any capability, and inject no initialization_script.

findings.claim: Current stable Tauri 2.x pieces: tauri 2.12.5 (tray-icon feature), tauri-build 2.7.4, global-shortcut 2.4.1, single-instance 2.5.4, opener 2.7.2, window-state 2.5.0, dialog 2.8.3, log 2.10.1. npm: @tauri-apps/api and @tauri-apps/cli 2.12.4, with JS plugin versions matching the crates. All are Apache-2.0 OR MIT, MSRV 1.90.
findings.detail: `cargo search` returns the 3.0.0-alpha versions (tauri-plugin-dialog 3.0.0-alpha.4 and others), so always request "2". Versions above come from `cargo info <crate>@2`. Tray: tauri feature tray-icon (depends on tray-icon 0.25.1). TrayIconBuilder::show_menu_on_left_click(bool), on_menu_event, on_tray_icon_event; TrayIcon::set_menu(Option<M>), set_tooltip, set_icon (tray/mod.rs:319-523); Menu::append/insert/remove (menu.rs:264-352); MenuItem::set_text/set_enabled. For a dynamic favourites list, rebuild the submenu and call set_menu. Image::from_bytes needs the image-png or image-ico feature. tauri default features: wry, compression, common-controls-v6, dynamic-acl, x11, dbus. single-instance on Windows (platform_impl/windows.rs): CreateMutexW("{identifier}-sim"); if ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, it FindWindowW("{id}-sic","{id}-siw") and sends argv and cwd via WM_COPYDATA. Callback FnMut(&AppHandle, Vec<String>, String). Optional features: semver, deep-link. It must be the first plugin registered. opener: open crate with feature shellexecute-on-windows (ShellExecute), so you get no process handle. window-state: with_denylist(&[&str]) matches exact labels, so use with_filter(|l| !l.starts_with("login-")); also skip_initial_state and with_state_flags. dialog: FileDialogBuilder add_filter, set_file_name, save_file(callback) or blocking_save_file() (only off the main thread, for example in an async command). global-shortcut: Builder::with_handler, with_shortcuts, on_shortcut and unregister_all.

findings.claim: Typed IPC: tauri-specta is still a release candidate in October 2026 (2.0.0-rc.26, 2026-10-21) and needs exact version pins. Recommended: ts-rs 12.0.1 for the shared types, plus one hand-written TypeScript file of typed invoke wrappers.
findings.detail: crates.io: tauri-specta max_stable 1.0.2 (Tauri v1 only), newest 2.0.0-rc.26. Its dependencies: specta =2.0.0-rc.26 (exact, while the latest specta is rc.27), specta-typescript ^0.0.13 (a caret on 0.0.x means exactly 0.0.13; the latest is 0.0.14, which is incompatible), tauri ^2, tauri-specta-macros =2.0.0-rc.26. Release history: rc.20 'Unlock Tauri Version' told users to pin tauri exactly; rc.21 (2025-01) was broken with released Tauri until a Tauri PR landed; rc.24 (2026-03-30) required =pins and changed generated bindings (serde phases; Builder::disable_serde_phases restores the old output); the gap from rc.21 to rc.24 was 14 months; docs.rs builds failed for rc.24 and rc.25. tauri 2.12.5 also has its own optional `specta` feature (specta ^2.0.0-rc.16). ts-rs 12.0.1 (2026-01-31, MIT, MSRV 1.78): #[derive(TS)] #[ts(export)]; `cargo test` writes ./bindings (or TS::export_all programmatically); env vars TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR, TS_RS_IMPORT_EXTENSION, TS_RS_LARGE_INT (default bigint, so set it to number or i64 IDs mismatch serde_json numbers). Features: serde-compat (default), uuid-impl, url-impl, serde-json-impl, chrono-impl and others. Reasons for ts-rs: stable semver, no exact pins, no coupling to Tauri releases; commands are only a few lines each to type by hand.

findings.claim: Storage: use rusqlite 0.40.2 with the bundled feature, plus rusqlite_migration 2.6.0. Skip rusqlite 0.41.0 (published today, 2026-10-24), which rusqlite_migration does not accept yet. refinery 0.10.0 and sqlx 0.9.0 are overkill for this app.
findings.detail: rusqlite versions: 0.41.0 (2026-10-24T10:35Z), 0.40.2 (2026-08-08, already in the local cache with libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2, which bundles SQLite 3.53.2), MIT, MSRV 1.89. Features include bundled, bundled-full, bundled-sqlcipher, bundled-windows. rusqlite_migration 2.6.0 (2026-05-28, Apache-2.0, MSRV 1.95) depends on rusqlite ^0.40.0; it tracks schema version with PRAGMA user_version (no extra table). refinery 0.10.0 (MIT, MSRV 1.92): refinery-core accepts rusqlite '>=0.23, <=0.40', is multi-backend and macro-based. sqlx 0.9.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, MSRV 1.94) is async and its compile-time query macros need DATABASE_URL or offline data. For a single-user desktop app, one rusqlite Connection behind a Mutex, called through spawn_blocking, is enough.

findings.claim: DPAPI in windows 0.62.2: CryptProtectData and CryptUnprotectData need the Win32_Security_Cryptography feature; LocalFree needs Win32_Foundation. Call with CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN (=1) and a null prompt struct, and free pDataOut.pbData with LocalFree after copying (and zeroing it, for unprotect output).
findings.detail: Signatures (windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/Security/Cryptography/mod.rs:1659,1872): CryptProtectData<P1: Param<PCWSTR>>(pdatain: *const CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB, szdatadescr: P1, poptionalentropy: Option<*const CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB>, pvreserved: Option<*const c_void>, ppromptstruct: Option<*const CRYPTPROTECT_PROMPTSTRUCT>, dwflags: u32, pdataout: *mut CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB) -> Result<()>; CryptUnprotectData(pdatain, ppszdatadescr: Option<*mut PWSTR>, poptionalentropy, pvreserved, ppromptstruct, dwflags, pdataout) -> Result<()>. CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB { cbData: u32, pbData: *mut u8 } implements Default. CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN: u32 = 1. Foundation: LocalFree(hmem: Option<HLOCAL>) -> HLOCAL. Call: LocalFree(Some(HLOCAL(out.pbData as _))). Microsoft docs (updated 2026-05-15): 'When you have finished using the DATA_BLOB structure, free its pbData member by calling the LocalFree function.' UI_FORBIDDEN: 'when this flag is set and a UI is specified... the operation fails'. 'The prompt-based flow controlled by this parameter is deprecated and will be removed in February 2027', so pass None. Only the same user can decrypt, normally on the same machine (a roaming profile is the exception). Do not set CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE.

findings.claim: argon2 0.6.0 and aes-gcm 0.11.x are new APIs. aes-gcm 0.11 removed generate_key(OsRng) and generate_nonce(&mut OsRng); argon2's defaults (19 MiB, t=2, p=1) equal the OWASP minimum. Use stronger settings for an offline vault key.
findings.detail: argon2 0.6.0 (2026-08-27; RCs ran through 2026; MIT OR Apache-2.0, MSRV 1.85). Params::new(m_cost: u32, t_cost: u32, p_cost: u32, output_len: Option<usize>) -> Result<Params>. DEFAULT_M_COST = 19*1024, DEFAULT_T_COST = 2, DEFAULT_P_COST = 1, DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LEN = 32. Argon2::new(Algorithm::Argon2id, Version::V0x13, params).hash_password_into(pwd, salt, &mut out) (needs the `alloc` feature). OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, Argon2id minimums: m=47104 (46 MiB) t=1 p=1; m=19456 (19 MiB) t=2 p=1; m=12288 t=3; m=9216 t=4; m=7168 t=5. Those minimums are for server-side password hashing. For a stolen-file KDF, prefer RFC 9106's second recommended option (64 MiB, t=3, p=4), or tune to about 0.5-1 s. aes-gcm 0.11.1 (2026-08-21, MSRV 1.85) docs: use aes_gcm::{aead::{Aead, AeadCore, Generate, Key, KeyInit}, Aes256Gcm, Nonce}; let key = Key::<Aes256Gcm>::generate(); let nonce = Nonce::generate(); cipher.encrypt(&nonce, pt). The example 'requires the getrandom feature'. The nonce 'MUST be unique per message'; use a random 96-bit nonce per encryption, stored with the ciphertext. zeroize 1.9.1 (MSRV 1.85), secrecy 0.10.3 (SecretString/SecretBox, ExposeSecret). Neither can scrub copies inside reqwest HeaderValue, WebView2 or SQLite pages.

findings.claim: reqwest 0.13.5: the default TLS is rustls with aws-lc-rs and rustls-platform-verifier (the Windows certificate store). The cookie store sits behind the opt-in `cookies` feature, so leaving that feature off means no jar exists. Cookie headers are stripped automatically on cross-host redirects. A default retry policy exists but only retries transport-level failures that are safe to retry.
findings.detail: reqwest-0.13.5/Cargo.toml: default = [default-tls, charset, http2, system-proxy]; default-tls = [rustls]; rustls = [__rustls-aws-lc-rs, dep:rustls-platform-verifier, __rustls]; rustls-no-provider is available for ring; cookies = [dep:cookie_crate, dep:cookie_store]; json, query and form are opt-in. Suggested: reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls","http2","charset","json"] }. Do not enable `cookies`. Set the cookie per request: .header(reqwest::header::COOKIE, format!(".ROBLOSECURITY={v}")). src/redirect.rs:239-251 remove_sensitive_headers: on a host, port or scheme change it removes AUTHORIZATION, COOKIE, cookie2, PROXY_AUTHORIZATION and WWW_AUTHENTICATE. Use redirect::Policy::none() on auth calls to see Location headers. src/retry.rs: 'The default retry behavior of a Client is to only retry requests where an error or low-level protocol NACK is encountered that is known to be safe to retry'; ClientBuilder::retry overrides it. aws-lc-sys 0.46.0 (cached) has prebuilt-nasm and disable-prebuilt-nasm features and already exists in this machine's cargo cache. A single shared Client is safe across accounts when no jar is enabled.

findings.claim: Supporting crates (latest stable on 2026-10-24): thiserror 2.0.21, tokio 1.54.1, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.154, uuid 1.29.0 (1.28.0 cached), url 2.5.8, percent-encoding 2.3.2, sysinfo 0.39.6, governor 0.10.4, cookie 0.18.2, keyring 4.2.0. Every MSRV is within the installed rustc 1.99.0, and no licence is a concern (all MIT or Apache-2.0).
findings.detail: From cargo search, cargo info and the cached Cargo.toml files: tokio 1.54.1 (MIT, MSRV 1.85; enable rt-multi-thread, macros, time, sync, process); uuid 1.28/1.29 (MSRV 1.89; features v4, serde); sysinfo 0.39.6 (2026-07-09, MIT, MSRV 1.95). sysinfo's default features include `component`, which pulls in the windows WMI/COM features; use default-features = false, features = ["system"]. governor 0.10.4 (2025-12-16, MIT, no MSRV declared) is the mature keyed limiter, but for a few Roblox endpoints that also need Retry-After/429 handling, a hand-written Mutex<HashMap<&'static str, Instant>> next-slot throttle with tokio::time::sleep_until is about 15 lines and needs no dependency. Recommended: write it by hand. rusqlite_migration is Apache-2.0 only, which is still permissive.

findings.claim: windows crate features for multi-instance work: CreateMutexW and CreateEventW sit in Win32::System::Threading but only compile with the Win32_Security feature as well. Each returns Result<HANDLE>; check GetLastError() == ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS right after a successful call. Open-source tools disagree on which Roblox singleton object matters.
findings.detail: windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/System/Threading/mod.rs:247-301: #[cfg(feature = "Win32_Security")] pub unsafe fn CreateEventW<P3>(lpeventattributes: Option<*const SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES>, bmanualreset: bool, binitialstate: bool, lpname: P3) -> Result<HANDLE>; same gate for CreateMutexW<P2>(Option<*const SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES>, binitialowner: bool, lpname: P2) -> Result<HANDLE>. Also ReleaseMutex; Foundation has GetLastError() -> WIN32_ERROR, ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS = WIN32_ERROR(183) and CloseHandle. Feature list: ["Win32_Foundation","Win32_Security","Win32_System_Threading"]. Keep the HANDLE alive for as long as the object must exist. Third-party evidence: MultiBloxy (github.com/Zgoly/MultiBloxy, last commit 2025-11-24), Program.cs:43 `mutexName = "ROBLOX_singletonEvent"`, creates a .NET Mutex with that name, and HandleCloser.cs closes 'ROBLOX_singletonEvent' handles in Roblox processes with DuplicateHandle(DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE). Its README warns that 'Roblox is actively blocking multi-instance tools'. Bloxstrap (bloxstraplabs/bloxstrap, last commit 2026-08-05) LaunchHandler.cs:226 calls Mutex.TryOpenExisting("ROBLOX_singletonMutex") for its launch-confirmation prompt. A secondary source (DeepWiki) says Fishstrap holds ROBLOX_singletonMutex in a watcher process; not verified in source, because Fishstrap's repository is not code-search indexed. Which object the current RobloxPlayerBeta checks is unverified.

findings.claim: Launching and watching for exit: when the exe path is known, std::process::Command or tokio::process::Command (raw_arg, creation_flags) is enough, and CreateProcessW adds nothing. To watch a process you did not spawn, use OpenProcess(PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + WaitForSingleObject on a blocking thread rather than polling by PID. For enumeration, sysinfo already wraps Toolhelp32.
findings.detail: Launching through opener or the roblox-player: protocol goes through ShellExecute and returns no handle (T8). tokio::process::Child::wait().await waits asynchronously (needs tokio feature process). std::os::windows::process::CommandExt::raw_arg avoids MSVC quoting of the URI argument. CreateProcessW (Threading:360) is gated on Win32_Security, takes Option<PWSTR> mutable command line, *const STARTUPINFOW and *mut PROCESS_INFORMATION; it is only needed for exotic flags such as CREATE_SUSPENDED. Constants: PROCESS_SYNCHRONIZE = 0x100000, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION = 0x1000, INFINITE = u32::MAX, WAIT_OBJECT_0, DETACHED_PROCESS, CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP. Also RegisterWaitForSingleObject, GetExitCodeProcess and QueryFullProcessImageNameW (all Threading). sysinfo 0.39.6 on Windows enumerates with CreateToolhelp32Snapshot (src/windows/system.rs:236). API: refresh_processes_specifics(ProcessesToUpdate::All, true, ProcessRefreshKind::nothing()), processes_by_exact_name(OsStr), Process::{wait(), parent(), start_time(), exe(), cmd(), kill(), exists()}; exe and cmd only load with the matching refresh kind. Calling Toolhelp32 directly needs the Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp feature (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32FirstW/NextW, PROCESSENTRY32W). Handle-based waits avoid PID-reuse bugs.

findings.claim: Toolchain on this machine: npx and plain bunx run @tauri-apps/cli 2.12.4 correctly. `bunx --bun` (Bun as the runtime) breaks the CLI's argument parsing. create-tauri-app runs and supports `-m bun -t react-ts`. cargo-tauri is not installed. Nothing was scaffolded.
findings.detail: Installed: node v26.4.0, npm 11.17.0, bun 1.3.14, rustc and cargo 1.99.0 (2026-09-28); targets x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, i686-pc-windows-msvc, wasm32-wasip2. `npx --yes @tauri-apps/cli@2.12.4 --version` → 'tauri-cli 2.12.4'. `bunx @tauri-apps/cli@2.12.4 --version` → 'tauri-cli 2.12.4'. `bunx --bun @tauri-apps/cli@2.12.4 --version` → "error: unrecognized subcommand '%USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin\bunx.exe'". `cargo tauri` → 'no such command'. npm dist-tags: @tauri-apps/cli latest 2.12.4, next 3.0.0-alpha.5. create-tauri-app latest 4.7.5 on npm, but the binary reports 4.8.0. Its --help lists -m/--manager [cargo, pnpm, yarn, npm, deno, bun, dotnet], -t/--template (react-ts and others), --identifier, -y, -f, --tauri-version [1|2]. The npm CLI (2.12.4) and the crate (2.12.5) agree on major.minor, which is all that needs to match. Checks ran in an empty scratch dir (clicheck), which is still empty.
sources: local shell checks 2026-10-24 (npx, bunx, npm view, cargo)

open_questions: Runtime check needed (T3/T4): does WebView2 CreateCookie with domain "roblox.com" (no dot) create a host-only cookie that www.roblox.com and *.roblox.com do not receive? Test in a dev build with a dummy, non-secret cookie, then read it back with GetCookies and see whether the stored domain is "roblox.com" or ".roblox.com".

Do concurrent incognito(true) webviews that share one data directory also share one InPrivate cookie jar? Inferred yes from Chromium's off-the-record design; not tested. The recommended design avoids the question by giving each window its own data_directory.
The exact WebView2 wording for the ERROR_INVALID_STATE environment-option mismatch was confirmed only through a search summary and a third-party mirror (opendlang), not the primary Microsoft page.

Which named kernel object the current RobloxPlayerBeta.exe uses as its singleton: MultiBloxy targets ROBLOX_singletonEvent, Bloxstrap checks ROBLOX_singletonMutex. Does Hyperion now detect pre-created objects? This belongs to the launch-flow topic.

Does launching RobloxPlayerBeta.exe directly (with the roblox-player: URI as its argument) give a handle to the long-lived game process, or does a launcher chain spawn the real process and exit? This decides whether Child::wait works or PID discovery plus OpenProcess is needed.
Does `bun run tauri dev` from package.json scripts honour the CLI's node shebang? Only `bunx --bun` was shown to break. Not run, to avoid scaffolding.

Does the WebView2 Evergreen runtime on target machines meet the minimums: 101.0.1210.39 for incognito, and an ICoreWebView2Profile2-capable version for clear_all_browsing_data? Very likely on Windows 11 but unverified.
design_implications: Pin Tauri 2.x explicitly: tauri = "2.12" (2.12.5), tauri-build = "2.7" (2.7.4), @tauri-apps/cli and @tauri-apps/api ^2.12.4. Plugins: global-shortcut 2.4.1, single-instance 2.5.4, opener 2.7.2, window-state 2.5.0, dialog 2.8.3. cargo search shows 3.0.0-alpha versions, so never take the newest automatically.

Login window: create it from an async command (never a sync one) with WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, "login-<uuid>", WebviewUrl::External(https://www.roblox.com/login)), then .data_directory(<app_local_data>/tmp-webview/<uuid>), .incognito(true), .devtools(false), .general_autofill_enabled(false). Then use with_webview to turn off the default context menu, browser accelerator keys and password autosave. Give no capability to login-* labels and add no initialization scripts.

Capture: a worker thread (spawn_blocking) polls webview.cookies_for_url(https://www.roblox.com/) every ~500-1000 ms for a non-empty .ROBLOSECURITY. on_page_load or on_navigation only wake the worker through a channel. Never call cookies*() inside webview hooks or sync commands.

"Open roblox.com as account X": a fresh temporary data_directory window; inject the cookie through with_webview using raw ICoreWebView2CookieManager CreateCookie(name, value, ".roblox.com", "/") with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax, then navigate. Do not use tauri's set_cookie, which strips the dot and swallows errors.

Cleanup: read BrowserProcessId through with_webview before destroy(). After closing, OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE) + WaitForSingleObject with a timeout, then remove_dir_all with retries. Sweep stale tmp-webview folders on startup. Keep the main UI in the default app_local_data_dir UDF, which must never be used for roblox.com.

App Cargo.toml must use webview2-com = "0.39" and windows = "0.62" (the same versions as tauri, wry and the plugins) with features [Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_Security_Cryptography, Win32_System_Threading]. Add Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp only if not using sysinfo.
Storage: rusqlite 0.40.2 (features bundled) + rusqlite_migration 2.6.0, one Mutex<Connection> called through spawn_blocking. Hold off on rusqlite 0.41 until rusqlite_migration supports it.

Secrets: wrap each cookie with DPAPI (CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, no prompt struct, optional app-specific entropy, LocalFree on the output). If an optional master password layer is added, derive the key with argon2 0.6 Argon2id at about 64 MiB / t=3 (the defaults are only the OWASP server minimum) and encrypt with aes-gcm 0.11 using Key::generate and Nonce::generate (getrandom feature), never the 0.10 OsRng API. Use secrecy 0.10 + zeroize 1.9 for in-memory hygiene, while noting the copies they cannot reach.

HTTP: one reqwest 0.13 Client with default-features=false and [rustls, http2, charset, json]. Never enable `cookies`. Send an explicit COOKIE header per request. Use redirect Policy::none() where Location matters, and a hand-written per-endpoint next-slot throttle that honours 429 and Retry-After instead of governor.

Typed IPC: ts-rs 12.0.1 (#[derive(TS)] #[ts(export)], TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR, TS_RS_LARGE_INT=number set in .cargo/config.toml [env]) plus a hand-written src/api.ts with one typed invoke wrapper per command. Do not take a dependency on tauri-specta RCs.

Processes: launch with tokio::process::Command (raw_arg for the URI) when the player exe path is known, so child.wait() gives exit notification. Otherwise discover with sysinfo 0.39.6 (default-features=false, features=[system], ProcessRefreshKind::nothing()) and watch with OpenProcess + WaitForSingleObject. Use the windows crate CreateMutexW/CreateEventW only for whichever singleton strategy the launch-flow research confirms.

Tray: tauri feature tray-icon (+ image-png). Rebuild the favourites submenu and call TrayIcon::set_menu on change. Route menu ids such as "fav:<uuid>" in on_menu_event. window-state should use with_filter(|l| !l.starts_with("login-")). single-instance must be registered first. Backup save/open uses dialog's blocking_save_file / blocking_pick_file inside async commands.
